October 31, 2026

Trump administration signals Iran strikes could resume day after Election Day

tags: war, politics
sources: @aaronparnas

The Trump administration has informed Gulf states, including Saudi Arabia and Qatar, that an intense but short round of strikes on Iran could begin as soon as the day after Election Day, November 4. The Strait of Hormuz remains not fully open and kinetic action has been paused in recent weeks. Senator Chris Murphy said a classified briefing on what a restarted war would look like described it as potentially devastating and said it would undermine the rule of law.

Federal judge appoints special master to probe DOJ statements over Trump golf course

tags: legal, politics
sources: @aaronparnas

Judge Ana Reyes held a hearing in Washington on whether a golf course Donald Trump wants built in the District can proceed, and is appointing a special master to examine whether the Justice Department and Department of the Interior have told the court the truth. The judge pointed to discrepancies between Trump's public statements and the account given to the court. The hearing also revealed plans for a seawall estimated to cost between $150 million and $400 million in public funds, which the Justice Department said has not been approved.

Courts block Trump efforts to pressure election officials and void ballots

tags: legal, politics
sources: @aaronparnas

A federal judge ruled the Trump administration cannot threaten election officials or seek to prosecute them, and the Ninth Circuit rejected an attempt to throw out roughly 20,000 ballots in California cast by alleged non-citizens. Separately, the Justice Department warned Oregon officials of possible jail time if voting-related records were not preserved. Oregon Secretary of State Tobias Read responded by correcting the department's misspelling of his name and telling it to read the Constitution.

Report details mistreatment of pregnant women in ICE detention

tags: immigration, health
sources: @aaronparnas

A report from the Marshall Project describes pregnant women with no criminal record held in Texas ICE detention centers for more than six months, facing malnutrition and inadequate prenatal care. One woman at the Bluebonnet Detention Center said she slept on the floor for two nights, waited 15 days for a prenatal vitamin refill, and was served chicken that was often pink, cold and watery. She developed high blood pressure and gestational diabetes and gained only 15 pounds by her third trimester, against a recommended 25 to 35 pounds.

Pentagon braces for roughly $400 billion below Trump's FY2027 budget request

tags: defence, politics
sources: @oafnation_actual

Pentagon officials are preparing for a defense budget around $400 billion below President Trump's $1.5 trillion request for fiscal year 2027, according to Politico. Sources said the request is effectively dead, with a contingency plan near $1.1 trillion taking shape. No cut is final, and the administration still publicly backs the full request.

Poland suspends head of Constitutional Tribunal as police secure court

tags: politics, legal
sources: @groundnews, @oafnation_actual

Poland's government suspended Bogdan Swieczkowski, president of the Constitutional Tribunal, after a rival judge ordered him and his deputy out for a month, and police entered the court grounds as protests erupted. Three protesters were detained and President Karol Nawrocki cut short a trip to Senegal. Prime Minister Donald Tusk defended the move as restoring the rule of law, while the Tribunal's leadership called it an unlawful takeover and opposition politician Zbigniew Ziobro called it a criminal attack on the constitutional order. The dispute stems from judicial changes made under the former Law and Justice government that drew EU fines over judicial independence.

Russian strikes cut power to about 280,000 Ukrainian households

tags: war, energy
sources: @oafnation_actual

President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said overnight Russian strikes left roughly 280,000 households without electricity, with about 200,000 homes affected in the Dnipro region and more than 80,000 in the Kyiv region. Strikes hit a Kyiv heat and power plant, four substations in Dnipro and a gas facility. Repair crews are working to restore power as winter approaches.

Trump administration prepares one of the largest expulsions of Afghans

tags: immigration, politics
sources: @oafnation_actual

The Trump administration plans to deport a group of Afghan immigrants to Afghanistan, with more than 150 people expected to be removed, according to Reuters and the New York Times. Dozens have been detained in Louisiana and the first flight is expected as early as Monday. Many of those facing removal left Afghanistan after the 2021 Taliban takeover.

ICE officer indicted over Houston SUV strike

tags: immigration, legal
sources: @oafnation_actual

Officer Mario Alberto Morales has been indicted on a charge of second-degree aggravated assault with a deadly weapon, according to Harris County District Attorney Sean Teare. Prosecutors say video shows Morales steering his SUV into Miguel Parra-Hernandez on October 10, breaking his leg in three places. ICE denied the strike was intentional. Morales faces two to 20 years if convicted.

Utah committee to pick secret buyer for mothballed coal plant sought by AI campus

tags: climate, tech, energy
sources: @carolinegleich

The coal units at the Intermountain Power Project near Delta, Utah stopped running last year when new gas units took over, but the Legislature barred their decommissioning and they have been kept in working order. On November 4 a committee will select a buyer from four bids, all covered by nondisclosure agreements, with state officials confirming to lawmakers that the offers cannot be seen by the public; the state has the final say and could buy the units itself. At least one data center developer in Delta has publicly said it wants the units to power a large AI campus, which currently has one small tenant. An open letter asks OpenAI, Anthropic, Microsoft, Google, Amazon and xAI to publicly commit not to lease computing at any campus powered by a restarted coal plant.

Alphabet sheds $510 billion in market value in worst one-day drop

tags: markets, tech
sources: @groundnews

Alphabet shares fell 12.6% after disappointing quarterly earnings, erasing about $510 billion in market value and contributing to a 1.4% decline in the Nasdaq Composite. Third-quarter revenue was $127.6 billion, up 25% from 2025, while profit fell 25% to $26.2 billion as advertising growth slowed and AI search features generated less revenue despite higher usage. Google Cloud revenue more than doubled to nearly $31 billion, but AI investments exceeded $50 billion, with spending surpassing revenue by $9.1 billion. The company said it is expanding advertising within its AI search products.

Oil majors report sharply higher profits amid war in Iran

tags: markets, energy
sources: @aaronparnas

ExxonMobil and Chevron both reported large increases in quarterly profits, attributed in part to the war in Iran. Chevron's earnings surged more than 180% year over year, and ExxonMobil's profits doubled.

Slotkin describes plan for signature accountability cases if Democrats win Congress

tags: politics, legal
sources: @aaronparnas

Senator Elissa Slotkin, recorded by a conservative outlet, said Democrats would pursue a list of "signature cases" beginning in January if they take one or both chambers of Congress. She said each committee would pursue cases involving what she described as egregious legal violations and corruption, citing the East Wing ballroom project, the reflecting pool, and $200 million at the Defense Department. She said she drew the approach from a visit to Budapest, where officials dealt with 16 years of alleged corruption after an authoritarian leader was removed.

Trump complains about campaigning as investigations loom after Tuesday

tags: politics
sources: @aaronparnas

At a rally in Daytona Beach, Donald Trump complained about having to hold rallies and said he wished he could stop, and has said publicly and privately that he wants to relax after more than 20 days on the campaign trail. Politico reported that weekend rallies were initially cancelled because Republican candidates are at risk of losing in Kansas and Iowa. He is said to be privately bracing for significant investigations of himself, his family and associates, along with subpoenas and large legal bills, with early turnout reported as high among Democrats, independents and Latino voters.

Michigan Proposal 2 would bar contractor and utility money in politics

tags: politics, elections
sources: @aaronparnas

Michigan voters will decide Proposal 2, a citizen-led ballot initiative to limit money in politics, alongside races for governor and the Senate. The measure would prohibit monopoly utilities such as DTE and Consumers Energy, and corporations holding more than $250,000 a year in government contracts, from donating to politicians. It would also require political advertisements, including online ads, to disclose who paid for them.

Elon Musk overtakes George Soros as largest US political donor of all time

tags: politics, elections
sources: @groundnews

A ranking of the biggest donors in US federal elections places Elon Musk first with $735 million, almost entirely to Republicans in the 2024 and 2026 cycles, surpassing George Soros at $530 million to Democratic and liberal groups. Michael Bloomberg ranks third with $493 million, followed by Miriam Adelson at $491 million, Richard Uihlein at $490 million, Timothy Mellon at $340 million and Tom Steyer at $331 million. Ken Griffin, Jeff Yass and Sheldon Adelson round out the list at $323 million, $311 million and $271 million respectively.

Altman says personal computers should not hold scarce memory chips

tags: tech
sources: @aaronparnas

OpenAI chief executive Sam Altman said that from a global allocation perspective it is "quite terrible" for everyone to have a share of the world's limited DRAM supply sitting in their own computers. He argued the memory would be better allocated to data centers.

California high-speed rail chief resigns over travel expenses investigation

tags: politics, government
sources: @groundnews

California High-Speed Rail Authority CEO Ian Choudri resigned following an investigation into consultant travel expenses, with the board appointing state Finance Director Joe Stephenshaw as interim president. An inspector general's report found $680,500, or 60% of consultant travel reimbursements between 2024 and 2026, lacked required advance approval, including $592,000 deemed unallowable, covering premium airfare, upgraded rideshares, visits to gyms, bars and escape rooms, cancellation fees and claims without receipts. Whistleblower records obtained by CBS California Investigates showed taxpayer-funded rides near Choudri's Folsom home and nearby restaurants and bars. Approved by voters in 2008, the project's estimated first-phase cost has reached $126 billion.

Ukrainian drone maker says long-range strikes no longer depend on SpaceX

tags: war, tech
sources: @oafnation_actual

Fire Point chief executive Iryna Terekh told Reuters the company's systems are built to complete missions without a satellite link, following a 10-day SpaceX slowdown this month. She said full Starlink access over Russia would be a "game changer." The company's FP-7 missile, with a range of about 300 kilometres, saw its first combat use this month.

Florida sting yields 281 arrests on trafficking and child predator charges

tags: legal, policing
sources: @aaronparnas

Law enforcement in Polk County, Florida made 281 arrests in an undercover human trafficking and child predator operation, according to CBS 12. The operation produced more than 480 charges, including 198 felony counts, and the sheriff described it as the largest ever conducted in the county. Among those arrested were 117 alleged sex buyers, 122 people on prostitution charges and 31 people arrested as child predators, including a youth football coach. Seventeen of those arrested worked at theme parks, including 13 at Disney and four at Universal Studios.

Retired professor arrested for blocking Uber Eats delivery robot plans First Amendment defense

tags: legal, tech
sources: @groundnews

Philadelphia police arrested Carolyn Marvin, a 78-year-old retired University of Pennsylvania professor, on October 14 after she blocked an autonomous delivery robot on a public sidewalk, charging her with disorderly conduct after a report of criminal mischief involving a robot. The robot belongs to Avride, which began an automated food delivery partnership with Uber Eats in Philadelphia in March. Marvin, a scholar of communication and First Amendment law, said her protest opposed the replacement of human delivery workers and the privatization of public sidewalks, and plans to challenge the charge on First Amendment grounds.

Newly released FBI files detail early Israeli influence networks in the US

tags: surveillance, politics
sources: @oafnation_actual

Records released on October 21 following a Freedom of Information Act request describe explosives procurement, shortwave communications and an Anti-Defamation League document channel during Israel's formative years, according to Military.com. The files come from the FBI's ISINT investigation into Israeli intelligence activity.

Air Force One flyover for White House party delays 202 flights

tags: government
sources: @oafnation_actual

An Air Force One flyover for a White House Halloween party delayed dozens of flights on Thursday evening, according to Reuters. The jet made two low passes around the White House, prompting the FAA to halt traffic at Reagan National Airport. The D.C. Council said officials received only 15 minutes notice, and FlightAware counted 202 delayed flights tied to the disruption.

Fitts says COVID pandemic was engineered as part of a financial reset

tags: economy, health
sources: @ericmoutsos

Catherine Austin Fitts argued that the COVID-19 pandemic and associated lockdowns were deliberately engineered as part of a long-running financial coup intended to shift both monetary and fiscal control to bankers. She said central banking systems carry out a reset every 80 to 120 years, and that lockdowns wiped out small businesses while five to six trillion dollars of injected money allowed large publicly traded firms to absorb their market share. She cited a statistic that 39% of US small businesses went under or bankrupt, and said inflation was initially masked by demand destruction before accelerating once businesses reopened.

NASA identifies 4.1-billion-year-old Martian meteorite found in the Sahara

tags: science
sources: @groundnews

NASA researchers identified a meteorite discovered in Mali's Sahara Desert in 2022 as one of the three oldest known pieces of Mars found on Earth. The nearly two-pound, rose-colored rock, named Teghaza 001, contains minerals that formed from cooling magma and were altered by water about 4.1 billion years ago, suggesting early Mars had a more active water cycle than previously understood. NASA scientist Yang Liu, who led the research, said a reviewer described the meteorite as "a Rosetta Stone for Mars."
